review.market_summary: 1) Nvidia shock: Jensen Huang has resigned amid a scandal over chips reaching China. Congress backs tighter export curbs, the Senate wants testimony from Huang and Commerce Secretary Lutnick, and the White House is reportedly weighing firing Lutnick. Money is moving out of NVDA (−8.5% over 5 days) and into its competitors (AMD +45%, LRCX +26%), so chips are not falling as a group. 2) Hawkish turn at the Fed: after a hot October CPI, Fed Governor Waller floated a half-point hike, a wholesale price (PPI) report is due that could tip the Fed further, Treasuries are having their worst week since 'liberation day', and the dollar is at a 19-month high. Stocks have shrugged this off so far (SPY +3.3%, QQQ +6.4%). 3) Iran and the US are trading strikes near the Strait of Hormuz (an attack on Sirik, then an Iranian strike on a US radar in Bahrain, then IRGC threats of a harsher response). Defense stocks have already rallied but crude has not.
